author: Priyanka Patel
title: Maloya Festival: 7 Years of Celebration | [Year]
text:
7th Annual Maloya Festival to Celebrate Réunion Island ‘s Vibrant Creole Culture A celebration of music, art, and tradition, the 7th edition of the Maloya Festival will take place from friday, September 5 to Sunday, September 7, 2025, on the Placette de Basse Terre in saint-Pierre, Réunion Island. The event, marking the 29th anniversary of the simangavol Association, is dedicated to bolstering Creole culture and fostering community spirit.
A Gathering rooted in Tradition At the heart of the festival grounds, volunteers will construct a unique “green room” woven from braided coconut leaves. This space, described as a symbol of gathering, will host the daily “Krasé Maloya” – informal improvisational sessions where artists and audience members connect through music, specifically the rhythms of the roulèr and kayanm , echoing the spirit of traditional long-ups .
The festival’s core mission remains steadfast: to bridge generational gaps, champion the creole language , honor local craftsmanship, and preserve the rich musical heritage of Réunion. Organizers are actively involving children and young people through collaborations with schools in Saint-Pierre and the continuation of percussion workshops held throughout the year.
Did you know? – Maloya music was once banned in Réunion due to its association with resistance against slavery. It was officially recognized as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural heritage in 2024. A Diverse Program of Events The three-day festival promises a diverse lineup of concerts and entertainment,all designed to uphold the values of Réunion Island. The festivities will kick off on Friday with a parade through the streets of Basse Terre, followed by performances from Mazad, Tessa Sega, Sega Dossier, Nout ‘Racine, and Sector 410.
Saturday will offer attendees the chance to immerse themselves in cultural and craft workshops , including traditional longan games, demonstrations of beef cart transport, and art exhibitions . The evening’s musical program features Foumb’e Maloya, Bea Lagarrigue, Zenes Tradisyon, Phil an Maloya, Kiltir, and Kaf la.
Sunday will be dedicated to honoring popular traditions with a horse-drawn carriage display, a domino tournament, and a ball featuring the Southern Tropical Orchestra.
Pro tip: – The roulèr ,a large,hollowed-out tree trunk,is the foundational instrument of Maloya music. Skilled players create complex rhythms by striking it with sticks. Beyond the music: A Hub for Community and Creativity The festival program extends beyond musical performances to encompass a wide range of activities. An “associative village” will be established in partnership with AREP, Local Mission, Synergie OI, and Synergie Family, aiming to raise awareness of social and professional support services available to the public.
Attendees can also explore a village showcasing the work of local painter artists, including Ti Danyel, Charlylesquelin, and Mme Malbrouke. Conferences and discussions will focus on Creole identity , while tastings of traditional dishes will highlight the island’s unique culinary heritage. An exhibition of longan objects will further celebrate local artistry. Live performances encompassing Maloya , Séga , and musical fusions will punctuate the event throughout each day and into the night.
